## Comment — @MauriceVanVeen (2026-02-19) [marked as answer]

Followed the guide and was able to push the account. Not sure what's different between your config and mine.

Looking at your server version:
```
Starting nats-server version 1.4.1
```
That's way too old! You'll need at least 2.2.0, which is also logged when creating an operator:
```
[ OK ] When running your own nats-server, make sure they run at least version 2.2.0
```

I'd highly recommend you upgrade to the latest 2.12.4 version.

---

I'd also recommend trying out a simple local setup for local dev if you're just starting out, that's as simple as `nats-server -js` to get a local server that's JetStream-enabled.

---

Admittedly the UX of `nsc` isn't the best still, and is one of the reasons for improving it as part of the new `nats auth` command. That makes it a lot simpler, I've successfully used the following steps:

```
# Create and select operator.
nats auth operator add MyOperator
nats auth operator select MyOperator

# Create account, user, and creds.
nats auth account add MyAccount --defaults
nats auth user add MyUser MyAccount --defaults
nats auth user credential MyUser.creds MyUser MyAccount

# SYSTEM account is pre-created, create user and creds for it.
nats auth user add sys SYSTEM --defaults
nats auth user credential sys.creds sys SYSTEM

# Generate server config (prompts for storage dir, etc.)
# Select: "'nats auth' managed NATS Server configuration"
nats server generate nats-auth-config

nats-server -c nats-auth-config/server.conf
```

```
$ nats auth account push MyAccount --creds sys.creds 
Updating account MyAccount (ADUE6YPH3JI5FLIZVAYMZ2BDGG2HJGIMPMAL4QZL34P3KQ6RWTVLFGE7) on 1 server(s)

✓ Update completed on nats.example.net

Success 1 Failed 0 Expected 1
```

```
# In one terminal.
$ nats sub '>' --creds MyUser.creds
16:41:22 Subscribing on > 
[#1] Received on "hello"
nil body

# In another.
$ nats pub hello '' --creds MyUser.creds
16:41:42 Published 0 bytes to "hello"
```

## Comment — @aricart (2026-02-19)

The main issue is your server version a Maurice pointed out. Likely that version doesn't support `$SYS.REQ.CLAIMS.UPDATE`
